solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Master struggling to divide pupils into ability groups

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of master thrashing about into a new order

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster finds it hard to sort a class into sets by ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges MASTER; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools, streaming is the practice of putting pupils into classes by ability.

clue.text: Bird out, unwisely perched on chimney pot

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece perched on another sits above it, so it comes first
unwisely suggests the word out has been put together in a careless, jumbled order

parts.note: a chimney pot is also called a can, the cylinder on top of a chimney

explanation.surface: A bird has carelessly settled on top of a chimney pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwisely' turns OUT into TOU; in a down entry 'perched on' puts TOU above CAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The toucan is a tropical bird with an enormous colourful bill.

clue.text: Newspaper proprietor headed his after a struggle

indicators.note: after a struggle suggests the words headed his come out of a tussle disordered

explanation.surface: A press baron took charge of his paper only after a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a struggle' rearranges HEADED HIS. Eddie Shah founded the British national daily Today in 1986 after a bitter dispute with the print unions.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie Shah is a British businessman who launched and owned newspapers, notably Today.

clue.text: Insect from swamp a silly boy brought in

indicators.note: brought in says one piece is placed inside the other
silly suggests the letters of swamp a are behaving foolishly and fall out of order

parts.note: a boy is a son

explanation.surface: A foolish lad drags a bug in from the marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges SWAMP A into MAWASP, and 'brought in' places the boy inside it; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason wasp is a solitary wasp that builds its nest from mud, like a little mason.

clue.text: Spray is not working, so discard

parts.note: a jet is a spray of liquid

indicators.note: working suggests the words is not being worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A spray nozzle has stopped functioning, so it gets thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' looks like one phrase meaning broken, but 'working' alone rearranges IS NOT into TISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw away or abandon something no longer wanted, originally cargo from a ship.

clue.text: Sailor on vessel gets top prize

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: Jack, short for Jack tar, is a familiar name for a sailor
a pot is a vessel for holding things

explanation.surface: A seaman aboard a ship wins the biggest award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship for the sailor, but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is the largest prize in a lottery or gambling game.

clue.text: Word describing element of heat

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round something, so one piece encircles the other

parts.note: a term is a word or expression

indicators.note: an element of a word here is its first letter, its opening component

explanation.surface: A clue asking for the word used for a measured amount of warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, a line drawn round a figure, so TERM goes round H, the first letter of 'heat' signalled by 'element of'. The whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat, used in Britain for billing gas, so the word names a measure of heat.

clue.text: Children's author almost upset dramatist

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read backwards
almost says the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children and other children's classics

explanation.surface: A writer for children is nearly overturned by a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims NESBIT to NESBI and 'upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Arranged to repeat a G&S production, perhaps

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of to repeat are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan show is set up for a revival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges TO REPEAT; the 'a' belongs to the definition. G&S is Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of comic operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote light comic operas, such as The Mikado, an example signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Copper left having made a careful inspection over in blind alley

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: over says the piece is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to case a place is to inspect it carefully, as a burglar does

explanation.surface: A policeman, having checked thoroughly, has gone down a dead end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is CU. 'over' reverses CASED to DESAC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is a street closed at one end, a dead end with no way through.

clue.text: Opening of exhibition, flower festival

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A flower festival is opened as part of an exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower festival' reads as one event; the flower is ASTER and 'festival' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection of Christ.

clue.text: Tease Oscar in shelter

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a haven is a place of shelter
Oscar is the radio alphabet word for O

explanation.surface: Someone mocks Oscar while they huddle under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: HAVE ON is a British idiom for teasing or fooling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is a colloquial way of saying to kid or pull their leg.

clue.text: Pardon me for breaking a pouncet

indicators.note: breaking suggests the words pardon me are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An apology for smashing a little perfume box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges PARDON ME; 'for' is a link. A pouncet-box, often shortened to pouncet, is a small perforated box for scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A pouncet-box was a small perforated scent case, the same kind of object as a ball of perfume carried against smells.

clue.text: One unit of highest quality

definitions.meaning: one as in the single spot on a playing card or die
a unit is a single point, as a point won in tennis or racquet games

explanation.definitionFit: An ace is the one in cards and dice, a single point scored, and in slang anything excellent.

clue.text: Toast with the dean as hall happens to collapse

indicators.note: to collapse suggests the words with the dean as hall happens falling apart and landing in a new order

parts.words: with the dean as hall happens

explanation.surface: Glasses are raised with the dean just as the college hall gives way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to collapse' rearranges all of WITH THE DEAN AS HALL HAPPENS, twenty-four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional toast wishes the company good bodily condition, prosperity and contentment.

clue.text: Sumo types with ones taking it easy round lake

indicators.note: round says the first piece goes about the other

parts.note: people who rest are resters

explanation.surface: Sumo practitioners lounge about beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: RESTERS goes 'round' L to give RESTLERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumo is a form of Japanese wrestling, so its competitors are examples of grapplers.

clue.text: Master at sea heading for Dubrovnik, a medium-sized port

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of master are muddled
the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A ship's captain sails for Dubrovnik and a modest harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master at sea' reads as a captain sailing, but 'at sea' rearranges MASTER into AMSTER. 'heading for' gives D, then A and M.
explanation.definitionFit: Amsterdam, the Dutch capital, is a major seaport on the IJ waterway.

clue.text: On the air, weird central character, say

indicators.note: weird suggests the letters of on the air are strangely scrambled

explanation.surface: A strange figure is being broadcast live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges ON THE AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An antihero is a protagonist lacking heroic qualities, one example of a story's main figure, as say signals.

clue.text: See 14
Tune from couple with no piano

indicators.note: with no says a letter is dropped

parts.note: a couple is a pair
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A duet played without a piano accompaniment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piano' is the musical marking p, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody or song.

clue.text: Approaching popular retail outlet

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Customers are heading towards a fashionable shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retail outlet' suggests a shop is being defined; the definition is 'Approaching'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in store is coming or imminent, about to happen.

clue.text: One's story upset tennis star

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the letters upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: I is one, so one's is I's
a saga is a long story

explanation.surface: Someone's tale knocks a tennis champion off balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the whole run, giving ISSAGA read back to front; the surface's tennis upset is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre Agassi is an American former world number one tennis player.

clue.text: The other woman showing tension on English motorway

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another comes after it

parts.note: the M1 is England's main north-south motorway, read as MI
stress is tension

explanation.surface: A mistress is frazzled while driving on an English motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 runs from London to Leeds; its numeral 1 is taken as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The other woman is a euphemism for a man's lover outside his marriage.

clue.text: Solicitor protecting right of grumpy old woman

indicators.note: protecting says one piece surrounds and shields the other

parts.note: a tout solicits custom, so he is a solicitor in the literal sense

explanation.surface: A lawyer stands up for a cantankerous old lady's rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but it is a tout who solicits business. Old trout is British slang for an irritable old woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout, usually old trout, is informal slang for a bad-tempered older woman.

clue.text: Who may have inspired poetry from reader at Oxford?

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Asks who was the source of a university lecturer's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' lifts the letters out of readER AT Oxford. A reader is a senior university lecturer.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, a goddess of inspiration.

clue.text: Article about English silver in a Melbourne newspaper

parts.note: the is the definite article
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A piece on English silverware appears in an Australian daily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is used loosely: THE is followed by AG and E rather than truly surrounding them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Age is a daily newspaper published in Melbourne, Australia.

clue.text: Girl carrying on in Valentine's place?

indicators.note: carrying says one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: Vera is a girl's name
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl is fooling around on Valentine's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: Valentine is one of Shakespeare's Two Gentlemen of Verona, not the saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Valentine is a hero of Two Gentlemen of Verona, so that city is his home.

clue.text: Take too much round Cape, having very large load

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: having means holding something inside

parts.note: Cape Verde, the island nation, gives the word that goes with cape
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: Someone sailing round a cape with a huge cargo takes on too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Cape Verde is the Atlantic island nation off West Africa; 'having' signals containment and 'load' just underlines that the outsize piece is carried inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdose is to take an excessive amount of a drug or medicine.

clue.text: Conservationists in gloomy Scottish resort

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: morose means gloomy
the NT, National Trust, is the British conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners are glum at a seaside town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity preserving historic houses and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Montrose is a coastal town in Angus, Scotland, with beaches and golf links.

clue.text: Top decoration got in action

indicators.note: got in says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a suit is a legal action
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A top medal was won during combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks like combat but is a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the top of a mountain, a highest point.
